rule: mixed: the "stored" restriction is handled correctly as a condition and the rule fires, but "future lighting" is turned into a kind of its own that is then asserted to be future — a kind and a property the sentence never states, since futurity can only be carried by a verb's tense here. Rewrite as "Stored mire-essence will feed lighting." so the futurity rides the verb, where it can actually be recorded.
texts: good. fires once per forming, with the cauldron, the Keepers, the storing and the clay vessels all covered.
good. the same fireable shape, and it correctly carries the essence that formed through to the essence that is kept.

mixed: the rule fires and covers the drawing, the tending and the stored essence, but "the Keepers" is read here as an anonymous group whose members are typed "keeper" and no name is recorded, whereas your other sentences record the Keepers as a named body — the two records will not join up. Rewrite as "Each Keeper draws stored mire-essence when that Keeper tends a lantern." so both the per-Keeper reading and the referent are explicit.

mixed: the feeding rule itself is fine, but "future" is promoted into a standing claim that lantern lighting in general is future, which the sentence does not say — the word only picks out which lighting gets fed, and a noun has no slot to carry futurity. Rewrite as "Stored mire-essence will feed lantern lighting." so the futurity sits on the verb, which can carry it.
